findings.title: Queries are interpolated twice in the sharding path (here and again in runSplitQuery)
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on every target, including request.filters. Each shard sub-request then goes through runSplitQuery, which this PR also changed to call applyTemplateVariables on every target. So each target is interpolated once up front and again per shard group. The updated test confirms this: it expects 5 calls where the old code made 1. applyTemplateVariables is not idempotent in general. Ad hoc filters may be injected into the expression a second time, producing duplicate label matchers or line filters. Template variable values that contain `$` or `[[...]]` get re-expanded. The extra work is repeated for every shard group and every time chunk. The fix is to interpolate in only one place, for example by having the shard path pass already-interpolated targets to an inner function that skips interpolation, or by dropping interpolation from the shard path now that runSplitQuery does it. If interpolation stays in the shard path, the shard code must still interpolate before it calls getSelectorForShardValues, because it needs the final selector.

findings.title: Test asserts the redundant interpolation count instead of guarding against it
findings.body: The test 'Interpolates queries before running' now expects applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times. That is 1 call in runShardSplitQuery plus 4 from the sub-requests going through runSplitQuery. The test hard-codes the double interpolation as correct behaviour and depends on the shard count. It will break whenever the shard grouping changes, and it would make it harder to remove the duplicate interpolation later. The mock of applyTemplateVariables also mutates the query in place, so it hides any non-idempotence problem when a query is interpolated twice.
